prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign CAPRICORN: a mountain goat's head seen from the front: a long narrow face with a small pointed beard, level ears, and two very long ridged horns that rise straight up from the brow and sweep back and outward in a wide open curve (long ridged ibex horns, NOT the tight round spiral horns of a ram). Behind the head, a single sharp snow-capped mountain peak.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, stepped mountain ridges, rock strata and small upright crystals spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. It is an animal: absolutely NO human face. Its face is calm and neutral with a steady level gaze: no open mouth, no snarl, no frown. The sign's nature shows only through form: tall ridged horns, a steady climb of stepped shapes, a broad firm base: patience, ambition, endurance, the summit reached one step at a time.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: bone white, slate blue, pine green, bronze brown. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
